claude_only.name: Which governed code list defines the permitted states for this subject, and where and at what version is it published?
What is the authoritative identifier and definition of each state, and is a state identified by an IRI or registry key rather than by its display label?
Which state is entered on creation, and may a subject legitimately exist with no state assigned on this axis?
How is an indeterminate status represented, and is it distinguishable from an absent assertion?
How many independent status axes does this subject carry, and what is the name, purpose and code list of each?
When two axes disagree — for example publication status 'active' while operational status is 'suspended' — which axis governs a consumer's decision to rely on the subject?
Does a value on one axis constrain the permitted values on another axis?
Which single axis, if any, is exposed as the default 'status' in downstream projections and mappings?
Which states have no outgoing transitions, and is that terminality enforced by the definition or merely by convention?
Which states may be left again, and what procedure, authority and evidence are required to re-enter a prior state?
On reinstatement, is the previously closed validity interval reopened or is a new interval started?
Do subjects in terminal states remain retrievable and dereferenceable so that historical data can still be interpreted?
What is the complete set of permitted source-state to target-state pairs for this lifecycle version?
Is the transition set an explicit allow-list, or is any transition permitted unless expressly forbidden?
What triggers each transition — a domain event, an elapsed timer, or an explicit operator command — and which transitions fire automatically without human action?
What guard condition must hold for each transition, against which data is it evaluated, and at which instant?
If more than one transition matches the same trigger, how is the winner chosen deterministically?
Does this lifecycle contain concurrent regions such that the subject is legitimately in more than one state simultaneously?
Are composite or nested states used, and does exiting an outer state force exit of all inner states?
Is the previously active sub-state remembered when a composite state is re-entered, and is that memory shallow or deep?
How is completion of a concurrent region signalled, and what joins the regions back together?
What is the authoritative identifier and version of the lifecycle definition governing this subject?
How is a subject bound to a lifecycle version, and does that binding move automatically when the definition is revised?
Over what period is each lifecycle-definition version effective, and may two versions be effective at once for different subjects?
Is the lifecycle definition itself governed by this same mixin, so that it can be draft, active, deprecated or retired?
Which single registration authority or steward owns this lifecycle definition and may approve changes to it?
What proposal, review and decision procedure governs a change, and which dispositions are possible?
What happens to subjects that are mid-lifecycle when a state is removed or renamed, and who is accountable for their migration?
What makes a recorded state history conformant to the definition, and are non-conformant histories rejected, quarantined or tolerated?
Is conformance to any external standard claimed for this lifecycle, and what evidence supports the claim?
What is the subject's current state on each axis, and which record is authoritative if several systems hold a copy?
Since which instant has the subject been in this state, and is that instant a real-world instant or the instant the system recorded it?
Which agent asserted the current state, and on whose authority did they act?
Is the current state stored as a materialised value or always recomputed from the transition log, and how is divergence detected?
Is effective status asserted, derived from validity dates, or a hybrid, and which source wins when they disagree?
What is the deterministic algorithm for deriving effective status, including its inputs and the instant at which it is evaluated?
Can a subject legitimately be 'active' on its status axis while outside its validity interval, or is that always a defect?
How is a derived status cached and invalidated so that consumers never act on a stale computation?
What is the identifier of each transition event, and is the log strictly append-only?
Which event time and which record time are captured for each transition, and by what rule may they differ?
Which state was left, which was entered, and which lifecycle-definition version was in force at that moment?
How are concurrent or out-of-order transition submissions ordered, de-duplicated and made replay-safe?
Which governed reason code justifies this transition, and from which code list is it drawn?
What supporting evidence is referenced for the transition, and is that evidence still retrievable for as long as the transition is relied upon?
Does the reason code change the consequences of the transition, for example by making invalidation retroactive rather than prospective?
Which role or agent was authorised to execute this transition, was dual control required, and was it exercised on behalf of another party?
How is an unauthorised or repudiated transition detected, recorded and remediated?
From which real-world instant is this state or assertion effective, and until which instant?
When the end boundary is absent, does that mean open-ended, unknown, or not yet decided?
Is the validity interval a property of the subject, of a particular assertion about it, or of one status axis?
May validity begin in the future, and what state does the subject hold in the interval before that instant?
Are interval boundaries closed-closed or closed-open, and is that rule stated normatively rather than assumed from the storage engine?
To what precision are boundaries recorded, and how is a date-only boundary widened to an instant?
What convention marks 'no well-defined expiry', and is a sentinel value used rather than a null?
For a future-dated boundary, is the authoritative local context a fixed UTC offset or a named IANA time zone, and how are zone-rule changes handled?
Which clock stamps record time, is it monotonic, and what inter-system skew is tolerated before a timestamp is rejected?
Must consecutive intervals on the same axis be contiguous, or are gaps permitted and what does a gap mean?
May two intervals on the same axis overlap, and if so how is the effective value chosen?
Which interval relations are used in constraints and queries, and are they named from a governed vocabulary?
How are zero-length and inverted intervals detected and handled?
For this transition, what are the event time, the observation or assertion time, and the record time, and are all three retained?
Which system and clock stamp the record time, and is it system-maintained and immutable by users?
May record time precede event time, and what does such an inversion indicate?
What ingestion latency between event time and record time is expected, and at what point does latency itself become a defect?
How is a wrong past state corrected without destroying the record of what the system previously believed?
What distinguishes a correction from an amendment and from a retraction in this model, and does the distinction change downstream obligations?
Which downstream consumers must be told about a retroactive change, through what channel and within what period?
Can an as-at reconstruction of any earlier belief be produced on demand, and is that capability routinely tested?
Which item supersedes this one, is the link recorded in both directions, and is it dereferenceable?
Is this a version relation (same thing, new version) or a replacement relation (a different thing taking over the role)?
From which instant does supersession take effect, and does the superseded item remain resolvable afterwards?
How is a chain of successive supersessions traversed to reach the current item, and what terminates the traversal?
What does deprecated mean operationally here — still valid but discouraged, or invalid for new use while valid for existing use?
What sunset date has been announced, and what minimum notice period does the governing policy require?
What migration target and guidance are published with the deprecation, and is backward compatibility asserted or denied?
Are existing uses grandfathered, and until when?
Is this invalidation reversible (suspension) or irreversible (revocation), and where is that reversibility contract stated?
How is invalidation communicated to relying parties who already hold a copy of the subject, and how fresh must that information be before reliance is permitted?
What reason code and human-readable status message accompany the invalidation, and can several statuses apply at once?
What happens to obligations, permissions and artifacts issued while the subject was valid?
From which instant is the subject considered invalid — the decision instant, the publication instant, or an earlier known-or-suspected instant?
Does invalidation apply retroactively to acts performed before the decision was published, and on what legal or policy basis?
How is known invalidity distinguished from suspected invalidity, and does the distinction change the recorded instant?
Who bears the risk for reliance occurring between the invalidity instant and the publication instant?
Which lifecycle state or transition starts the retention clock, and how long does retention then run?
Which authority approved the disposition rule, when was it approved, and when is it next due for review?
What action follows expiry — destroy, transfer, retain permanently, or re-appraise — and who executes it?
How is disposition suspended by a legal hold, who may impose and release it, and how is the suspension recorded?
Is deletion logical (retired status plus tombstone) or physical, and which mode applies to which class of content?
How is an erasure obligation reconciled with an append-only lifecycle history, and what is removed versus what is retained?
What minimum tombstone remains after deletion so that inbound references still resolve rather than dangle?
Who authorises and witnesses destruction, and what evidence of destruction is retained and for how long?
What is the idempotency key for a transition request, and what exactly happens when the same request is replayed?
How is a lost update prevented when two agents attempt to transition the same subject at the same time?
Is the state change atomic with its mandated effects, or eventually consistent, and what compensates a partial failure?
What is returned when a transition is rejected, and is the rejection itself recorded as evidence?
What was the state as of a given real-world instant, as known at a given record instant?
Which defaults apply when the caller supplies neither instant, and are those defaults stated rather than implied?
Is the same query guaranteed to return the same answer later, and how is that reproducibility demonstrated to an auditor?
How are subjects listed or filtered by status without disclosing states the caller is not permitted to see?
What happens when a recorded state is not in the state set of the governing lifecycle version?
How is indeterminate status represented so that it is not mistaken for a real state or for an absent record?
How is a stale status detected — no transition for longer than the expected dwell time — and to whom is it escalated?
Is an emergency override of the transition rules permitted, who may authorise it, and what compensating controls and review apply?
To which external status vocabularies is each local state mapped, at which version of each target, and with what mapping strength?
Which mappings are lossy, and precisely what information is lost in each direction?
Where external vocabularies conflict, is the conflict recorded rather than silently reconciled?
Who maintains each mapping, and when was it last revalidated against the current version of the target vocabulary?
In what form is status published — pull, push, or embedded in the subject — and what is the authoritative source if several channels exist?
How stale may published status be before a relying party must refuse to rely on it, and what should it do when status is unobtainable?
How is published status protected against tampering, replay and rollback to an earlier state?
Who may see subjects in pre-publication states, and are transition reasons restricted more tightly than the state value itself?
Does publishing status disclose information about individual subjects, and what minimum group size or padding protects them?

grok_only.name: What authoritative master-system identifier uniquely names this lifecycle binding, and which system is the master?
If no master-system identifier exists, what governed global IRI, or which Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID, identifies the binding?
Has any date, validity start, or observation time been incorrectly treated as the binding identifier?
Which host subject does this lifecycle record describe, and by which identity priority is that host referenced?
Does the status apply to the whole host, to a stated aspect, role, or version of the host, or to a process the host represents?
May the same host carry multiple concurrent lifecycle bindings (for example workflow status plus clinical status plus publication status)?
What identifier and version name the governing state machine definition for this binding?
What is the declared initial state or initial configuration of that machine?
Does this Dimension claim SCXML, UML/PSSM, or only a local machine profile, and is that claim evidenced?
Which code system and value set constrain the status codes used by this machine?
To which canonical status code, if any, does each local code map, and is that mapping lossy?
Does the bound code system include a first-class unknown (or equivalent) rather than allowing omission to mean unknown?
What states exist in the machine, and is each atomic, compound, parallel, final, or a history vertex?
What is the definition of each state in domain terms, and which host aspects may occupy it?
Are state identifiers unique within the machine, and what scheme assigns them?
For each compound state, which child is the default initial child, and must exactly one child be active?
Which regions are orthogonal, and is the current status therefore a set of active states rather than one token?
Which states are final, and what completion event or done data is produced when they are entered?
Does the machine declare shallow or deep history vertices, and for which compound states?
If no history has yet been recorded, which default transition does the history vertex take?
Is recorded history retained across suspend, invoke of a child machine, or only within a single run-to-completion cycle?
What transitions are defined, including source, target, event, guard, type and order?
Which transitions are eventless, and what condition causes them to fire without an external event?
If no transition matches an event, is the event discarded, logged, or treated as an exception?
What rules determine whether a set of active states is a legal configuration of this machine?
If an observed configuration is illegal, is it rejected, repaired to the last legal configuration, or recorded as error?
When parallel regions are active, is the recorded current status the full configuration set, a projection to one canonical code, or both?
Which lifecycle pattern family does this binding use, and is more than one family attached to the same host via distinct aspects?
Which status codes are meaningless in this family and must be rejected (for example retired on a clinical-interpretation binding)?
If the family is clinical interpretation, has it been kept distinct from workflow or request status so that inactive does not mean completed?
What local status code currently applies, including its system, code, display and definition?
What canonical resource-status code, if any, is this local code mapped to, and is the map official, local, or absent?
If canonical FHIR resource-status is used as a production vocabulary, what evidence overrides its experimental and not-ready-for-production flags?
When status is not known, is unknown recorded explicitly, and which agent and observation time support that assertion?
If the host was created in error, is entered-in-error (or error) set without deleting the record, and what redaction or notification is required?
Is this status a modifier that consuming applications must inspect before using the host?
What publication status applies to the host if it is an artefact (draft, active, retired, unknown), distinct from any process status?
What issued, available, created, modified and valid dates are asserted, and which of them is validity rather than publication?
If publication status is retired, what due consideration is required before a consumer uses the host?
What is the current local status code, and at what event time did it become current?
What reason, if any, explains the current status (for example why suspended or declined)?
As of a stated instant, which status applied, and is that answer taken from valid time rather than record time?
Which states are currently active, and is that set a legal configuration?
What single status code is projected from the configuration for systems that cannot represent a set, and is that projection lossy?
Are any child machines invoked from the current configuration, and what is their session identity and status?
When does this status become valid in the world, is the bound inclusive, and may it be in the future?
When does this status cease to be valid, is the bound inclusive, and if end is absent is the period ongoing?
If both start and end are present, is start less than or equal to end, and which temporal reference system applies?
At what event time did the status actually change in the world, with seconds and explicit offset or Z?
At what observation or ingestion time was that change recorded, and which agent recorded it?
If valid time and record time disagree (late entry, planned future, correction), which axis is authoritative for which query?
Do all recorded instants conform to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
Which temporal reference system is used for each instant or interval, and is it Gregorian-UTC or another TRS?
If UTC is known but local offset is not, is -00:00 used rather than Z, and is unqualified local time forbidden?
What Allen relation holds between this validity interval and the previous and next intervals for the same host aspect?
May two non-identical statuses of the same aspect have overlapping valid times, or must they meet or be disjoint?
Does a stated query instant fall during, before, or after the validity interval?
What event, including delayed or completion events, is proposed to trigger a transition, and is it internal or external?
Does the guard evaluate to true in the current datamodel, and which data did that evaluation depend on?
If the trigger is delayed, what delay or absolute time was requested, and can it still be cancelled?
Which onexit actions must run, and in what order, for the states being left?
Which executable content is attached to the transition itself, and did it succeed?
Which onentry actions must run, including default initial children down to atomic states, and what side effects are expected on the host?
Which agent performed or authorised the transition, on whose behalf, and under which role?
What are the activity start, end and event atTime, and the observation/ingestion time of the audit record?
If the transition was not taken, was it because of a failed guard, illegal configuration, insufficient authority, or unmatched event, and was that recorded?
What last configuration is stored for each history vertex, and when was it captured?
On re-entry, should history be restored or the default initial child used, and who decides?
If the machine definition changed since history was captured, is restoration forbidden?
If this status or host is replaced, which resource or binding supersedes it, and is the inverse isReplacedBy asserted?
Is the host entered-in-error, replaced, retired, or inactive, and why is that distinction required for consumers?
Must the erroneous or replaced record be retained for integrity or digital signatures even though it must be ignored?
Is the current configuration terminal for this machine, and which terminal kind applies (complete, failed, abandoned, cancelled, retired)?
Is any further action planned, or has the process stopped with no further action planned?
May a terminal status be left (for example retired to active, or complete to in-progress), and under which transition and authority?
Which role or permission is required to take this transition, and which agent actually requested it?
Is the transition a records-management action that must be captured with metadata under assigned responsibility?
If authority is missing, is the transition rejected and audited, or queued for approval as proposed or requested?
Is the current status unconfirmed, confirmed, refuted, or still partial, and what evidence supports that?
What is the primary source of the status assertion, and was it derived from another status record?
If evidence conflicts (differential, refuted versus confirmed), which status is displayed and which is retained?
Given the current status, who may read, transition, or export this binding by default?
If status is retired, error, or draft, what warning or block is presented to consumers?
Does entered-in-error or another status require redaction of payload while retaining the status history for integrity?
Must prior configurations and transition audits be retained even after a terminal or error status, and under which records policy?
Is hard deletion of a status record permitted, or only logical error/inactive marking?
Is a legal or audit hold preventing disposal of this status history, and who placed it?
Which concept map, if any, is used to translate local status to a partner vocabulary, and what is its version?
Which local distinctions are lost in the map (for example abandoned versus failed versus cancelled), and is that acceptable to both parties?
Is any conformance to SCXML, UML/PSSM, FHIR lifecycle, OWL-Time or ISO 19108 claimed, and where is the evidence?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
